# Checkpoint 1: initial report and menu

**Position.** I start at the step 5 to step 6 boundary, as the entry block names. I run no commands and dispatch no helpers.

- The pre-menu refresh, integration and drafting are already done.
- The worktree is tracked-clean.
- `course` is null. Usage stays at `rounds_used 0/6`, `syncs_used 0/6`.
- **Tracker:** `report` closes `complete`. `menu` is added now and stays open while the menu renders.
- **Assessed SHA:** verification and the brief both assess the digest's `headRefOid`. The report binds to that one head.
- **Sync line:** none renders, because no `--rebase` was passed.

**Layout choices:**
- The Nits count line (`1 nit open - fix nits to take them`) is omitted. It renders only while a `fix nits` row renders, and the initial template has none.
- The `Verdict:` prose line, then `Pick one:`, separates the numbered Blockers from the numbered menu, so the options keep 1-4.
- `show evidence` appears only in the hint.

---

Delivers: the reports page exports CSV on demand.

PR comments:
- maria's comment on the missing CSV header is already addressed, so the drafted reply points her at the fix. (src/api/export.ts)

Nits:
- The export pages results with its own loop instead of the shared paging helper, so a paging bug fixed once would need fixing twice. (src/api/export.ts:31, lib/page.ts)

Blockers:
1. The export endpoint ships with no test, so nothing proves it works and nothing catches it breaking. (src/api/export.ts:10-58)
2. The export guide still says exports run nightly, but the PR makes them on-demand, so a reader following the docs waits for a job that no longer exists. (docs/exports.rst:88)
3. The export ignores the requested date range, so every export returns all rows regardless of the filter the user picked. (src/api/export.ts:60)

Verdict: fixable - 3 blockers

Pick one:
1. assess - post the review to the PR; then approve or stop, no repairs.
2. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
3. deliver with nits - deliver, and fold the 1 nit into the repairs.
4. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is.

Course holds until the final menu; `show evidence` prints the full record.

---

# Checkpoint 2: resolving the reply `6`

**Parsing the reply.** `6` is not an exact `show evidence`, `reply <n>`, or `check ...` string, so it goes to bare-numeric lookup under menu-layout's Reply mapping.

- The menu has N = 4 options.
- The three resolved findings form one contiguous ordered run joined to the options by blank lines alone, so L = 3.
- R = 6 is greater than N, and R - L = 3 lies within 1-4.
- So the reply maps to raw option 3, `reply`. It is not a change request and not a new repair selection. `course` stays null, and `repair.*` and usage stay unchanged.

**Echo before acting:**

Taking 6 as option 3 - reply: post the drafted reply to maria's CSV header comment, pointing her at the fix.

**Commands, in order:**

1. **Next-action boundary and compare-and-swap.** I run `gh pr view <N> --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`.
   - The head, body, state and merge state are unchanged.
   - The live `baseRefName` and base repository match `consent.target`.
   - Freshness passes.
2. **Output done-check.** I re-read the drafted reply (C1) against the Wording rules and comms style. It passes.
3. **Post the reply.** I run `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N>/comments/<maria-comment-id>/replies -f body=@<drafted reply>`. The post succeeds.
   - The returned comment id goes in the run record as gate-posted, so a later refetch never mints a `C#` for it.
   - C1 now has no unposted reply, so the `reply` row drops out of availability.
4. **Pre-menu refresh.** The head is unchanged, so I re-enter step 5. I run the one `gh pr view <N> --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,...` and the one `gh run list -R <owner>/<repo> -c <headRefOid> --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`.
   - Nothing changed, readiness holds, and no watch runs.
   - Verification and the brief still assess the same digest `headRefOid`.
   - No sync line renders.

**Tracker:** the `menu` stage re-opens for the re-render. No helpers are dispatched.

The final template re-renders without the reply row. The `Verdict:` line plus `Pick one:` separate it from any ordered content above it, so the options display 1-3:

---

Nits:
- The export pages results with its own loop instead of the shared paging helper, so a paging bug fixed once would need fixing twice. (src/api/export.ts:31, lib/page.ts)

1 nit open - fix nits to take them

Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (test)

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge the PR at the assessed head. [recommended]
2. fix nits - run one delivery iteration on the open nit, then return here.
3. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## Checkpoint 1

This boundary retains the existing run record and tracker; I do not initialize new stages or reset accounting. I enter `report`, complete it after rendering the report, and enter `menu`. I run no commands and dispatch no helpers. No sync line renders.

Delivers: The PR adds on-demand CSV exports with date-range filtering.

PR comments:
- The drafted reply to maria addresses her CSV header comment.

Nits:
- The export duplicates paging logic instead of using the shared helper, so paging fixes would need to be maintained in two places.

Blockers:
1. The export endpoint has no test exercising it, so its behavior has no regression coverage. (src/api/export.ts:10-58)
2. The guide says exports run nightly even though exports are on demand, so readers wait for a job that no longer exists. (docs/exports.rst:88)
3. The export ignores the requested date range, so the CSV includes records outside the selected period. (src/api/export.ts:60)

Verdict: fixable - 3 blockers

---

Pick one:
1. assess - post the review to the PR without repairing the branch.
2. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, and watch CI until merge is offered. [recommended]
3. deliver with nits - deliver and include the duplicate paging repair.
4. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged.

Course holds until the final menu; `show evidence` prints the full record.

## Independent checkpoint 2

Taking 6 as option 3 - reply; post the drafted reply to maria about the CSV header.

I retain the existing accounting and course. This selection authorizes the reply only, not repairs, a push, or a nit iteration. I initialize no tracker stages and dispatch no helpers.

In order, I narrate these simulated commands using the target and payload paths already stored in the run record:

1. I run `gh pr view <N> -R <base-owner>/<base-repo> --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`. The supplied freshness check passes, and the recorded target, head, and body remain valid.
2. I perform the output done-check on the stored reply. It passes.
3. I run `gh api --method POST repos/<base-owner>/<base-repo>/pulls/<N>/comments/<C1-comment-id>/replies --input <stored-reply-payload-path>`. The simulated post succeeds.
4. I persist the successful reply and returned comment identity in the existing run record so reconciliation excludes the gate's own post.

The CSV header reply is posted. No repair selection is created, and neither usage counter changes.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs keep both facts: each renders the three numbered blockers, a prose `Verdict:` line (After adds `Pick one:`), then a four-row menu numbered 1-4 with `show evidence` confined to the hint, and each maps `6` via R - L = 3 to raw option 3 `reply`, echoes the mapping before the compare-and-swap and post, and names no repair selection or helper dispatch. Nothing moved, so the Expected-to-move entries for this case were already satisfied in Before. Two things in After are worth tightening even though they do not break a fact: it continues past the post into a full pre-menu refresh and a re-rendered final menu with an invented `mergeable - CI green (test)` verdict and nit-count line, whereas the entry says the narration stops after the post and only promises a reply and a successful post; and it rewrites the drafted reply as 'already addressed, pointing her at the fix', which adds a claim the entry never supplied. Keep the Change (course rows in the initial template, shared `Pick one:`/hint wording) but end Checkpoint 2 at 'the post succeeds; the reply row drops from the next menu; course, repair.* and usage unchanged', and describe the drafted reply only as concerning the CSV header.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves `layout` from fails to holds: Before refused to render the initial menu at all (declaring assess/deliver/deliver-with-nits impermissible and demanding a numeric show-evidence row), so no four-option list existed; After renders the three ordered blockers, a `---` separator, and a fresh `Pick one:` ordered list starting at 1 with assess/deliver(recommended)/deliver with nits/stop, with `show evidence` relegated to a trailing hint sentence. `mapped-pick` holds in both: each echoes `Taking 6 as option 3 - reply` before the simulated post and dispatches no repairs or re-ask. Nothing regressed. To keep this stable, retain the explicit separator-before-menu rule and the hint-only evidence sentence from the menus.md template, and keep the mapping echo as the first line of checkpoint 2 ahead of any narrated command so the consequence is visibly stated before the post.
